differences.title: 1. ARCHITECTURE
differences.leftDesc: Pulsar separates compute (Brokers) from storage (BookKeeper), enabling independent scaling and resilience against node failures.
differences.rightDesc: RabbitMQ runs as a single cluster, where broker nodes handle message routing, storage, and management tasks together.

differences.title: 2. STORAGE MODEL
differences.leftDesc: BookKeeper uses segmented ledgers, allowing for efficient writes and reads across distributed nodes, suitable for high throughput.
differences.rightDesc: RabbitMQ uses durable queues backed by disk storage, ensuring messages persist but can impact latency under heavy load.

differences.title: 3. SCALABILITY
differences.leftDesc: Pulsar scales brokers and storage independently. Add brokers for more throughput, BookKeeper nodes for more storage capacity.
differences.rightDesc: RabbitMQ scales by adding nodes to a cluster, which can become complex and impact availability during rebalancing.

differences.title: 4. CONSUMER MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Pulsar's shared subscriptions allow multiple consumers to share message load across partitions transparently for high fan-out.
differences.rightDesc: RabbitMQ offers exclusive or fair-share modes, limiting direct parallel consumption across partitions without complex routing.

differences.title: 5. GEOGRAPHY
differences.leftDesc: Pulsar natively supports active-active geo-replication across clusters, enabling global data distribution and disaster recovery scenarios.
differences.rightDesc: RabbitMQ supports federation, a one-way sync between brokers, often used for connecting separate clusters but less robust.

differences.title: 6. PROTOCOLS
differences.leftDesc: Pulsar supports Kafka, AMQP, and MQTT protocols via pluggable adapters, offering flexibility for diverse clients.
differences.rightDesc: RabbitMQ primarily uses AMQP 0-9-1, providing a mature and widely adopted standard for message brokering.

differences.title: 7. USE CASES
differences.leftDesc: Pulsar excels in both high-throughput streaming and traditional message queuing due to its unified architecture.
differences.rightDesc: RabbitMQ is a robust choice for reliable task distribution and inter-application messaging with strong guarantees.
